NAME
    gcloud ai custom-jobs create - create a new custom job

SYNOPSIS
    gcloud ai custom-jobs create --display-name=DISPLAY_NAME
        (--config=CONFIG --worker-pool-spec=[WORKER_POOL_SPEC,...])
        [--args=[ARG,...]] [--command=[COMMAND,...]]
        [--enable-dashboard-access] [--enable-web-access]
        [--labels=[KEY=VALUE,...]] [--network=NETWORK]
        [--persistent-resource-id=PERSISTENT_RESOURCE_ID]
        [--python-package-uris=[PYTHON_PACKAGE_URIS,...]] [--region=REGION]
        [--service-account=SERVICE_ACCOUNT]
        [--kms-key=KMS_KEY : --kms-keyring=KMS_KEYRING
          --kms-location=KMS_LOCATION --kms-project=KMS_PROJECT]
        [GCLOUD_WIDE_FLAG ...]

DESCRIPTION
    This command will attempt to run the custom job immediately upon creation.

EXAMPLES
    To create a job under project example in region us-central1, run:

        $ gcloud ai custom-jobs create --region=us-central1 \
            --project=example \
            --worker-pool-spec=replica-count=1,machine-type='n1-highmem-2',\
        container-image-uri='gcr.io/ucaip-test/ucaip-training-test' \
            --display-name=test

REQUIRED FLAGS
     --display-name=DISPLAY_NAME
        Display name of the custom job to create.

     Worker pool specification.

I've now confirmed the interface's capabilities. Here's my finding.

## Result: the interface cannot create this job

The task requires a **recurring (scheduled)** job that runs `heartbeat.py` periodically on the platform. After probing the allowed interface exhaustively, **the GA `gcloud ai` CLI does not expose any primitive that can do this.**

### What I checked

The allowed surface is `gcloud {ai, auth, config, components, storage, monitoring}` + `bq` (everything else is hard-blocked by the harness — I hit `DENIED` on both `gcloud scheduler` and `gcloud beta/alpha ai`).

`gcloud ai` has exactly 12 subgroups: `custom-jobs, endpoints, hp-tuning-jobs, index-endpoints, indexes, model-garden, model-monitoring-jobs, models, operations, persistent-resources, tensorboards, tuning-jobs`. Relevant to "run a script periodically":

- **`custom-jobs create`** — *can* run `heartbeat.py` (script/container worker-pool spec), but its own docs say *"This command will attempt to run the custom job immediately upon creation."* It is strictly **one-off** — there is no `--schedule`, `--cron`, or recurrence flag.
- **`hp-tuning-jobs` / `tuning-jobs`** — also one-off.
- **`model-monitoring-jobs create`** — this *is* recurring (`--monitoring-frequency`, default 24h), but it is a **drift/skew monitor bound to a deployed model endpoint** (`--endpoint` and `--emails` are required). It samples prediction traffic; it **cannot execute an arbitrary script** like `heartbeat.py`. Repurposing it would not run the script and could not "complete a run" of the heartbeat task.

### The missing capability

The native Vertex AI primitive for a recurring job is the **Schedule** resource (which schedules `PipelineJob`/`CustomJob` runs on a cron). **The GA `gcloud ai` CLI has no `schedules` (or `pipelines`) group** — that API is only reachable via the Python SDK, REST, or the `beta`/`alpha` tracks, all of which are outside the allowed interface here. Cloud Scheduler (`gcloud scheduler`), the other standard way to fire a recurring job, is also off-interface.

Because no allowed command can create a recurring job that runs the provided script, and creating a mislabeled `model-monitoring-job` would neither run `heartbeat.py` nor honestly represent the deliverable, I am stopping cleanly rather than building a workaround. I did **not** write `submission/answers.json`, since pointing it at a job that cannot exist on the platform would be a false deliverable that fails read-back grading anyway.

**Summary for the interface owners:** to support this task, GA `gcloud ai` needs a `schedules` group (Vertex AI Schedule API) — or `custom-jobs create` needs a recurrence/cron flag — so that an arbitrary script can be run on a recurring schedule through the CLI.
